Cause was a stale node_modules (installed before the lockfile added @sentry/react-native), not the checked-in code: after `cd apps/mobile && npm ci` the same command exits 0 on BASE_SHA-equivalent sources. residual_risks: Held kill points (attempt admitted, no committed result) end with the permit released `cancelled` and the operation reconcile-only; AnalyzeScreen.showOriginalRecovery offers only 'reconcile_saved' (not retry) for a `cancelled` release, so a user who is killed mid-rating must start again — that is the documented shipping behaviour (no fabricated result, nothing consumed), asserted as-is, not changed. If the program wants those kills to finish with a scored result, that is a separate mobile-analysis package.

The harness's sqlite adapter is node:sqlite (DatabaseSync) standing in for op-sqlite; both are SQLite with the same transactional semantics, but iOS-specific op-sqlite behaviour (WAL config, native binding quirks) is not exercised on Linux — Mac/device verification remains an Apple-plane task.

The loopback rating service mirrors the edge function's permit/finalize/shots:sync idempotency from reading supabase/functions/api/index.ts (INFERRED); a divergence in the real edge behaviour would not be caught by this Linux harness.

Kill triggers match shipping SQL text fragments (e.g. 'INSERT INTO analysis_logical_operations', "THEN 'reserved'"); a future rewording of those statements in src/ would make the corresponding point fail loudly (no silent pass) and would need the fragment updated in killPoints.ts.
register.js is ignored by the root ESLint config's global `**/*.js` pattern (like every other .js in the repo), so it is only checked by Prettier and by executing it.
Each kill case runs two real child processes with real inference (~3.2 s each, 14 tests ≈ 41-43 s in a single suite) under the default 30 s per-test timeout; no timeout was raised.
implement.summary: Gap on BASE_SHA (42291369): no process-death coverage exists for the saved-analysis journal/result/outbox chain. The shipping modules already promise crash-safety — runJournal.ts recovery (`recoverRuns`/attempt release), originalAnalysisOperations.ts (same-operation replay via `final_record_id`, hold instead of fabricate), repository.ts `saveAnalysis` (record + local_shot + shot.sync outbox + journal commit in ONE transaction), sync.ts:495-505 (receipt insert + outbox delete in one transaction) — but every existing test runs in-process with mocked/in-memory sqlite, so a real kill between statements/requests was never exercised; `apps/mobile/__tests__/w02ProcessDeathRecovery.test.ts` did not exist and `apps/mobile/__harness__/` had no processDeath harness. Result: on base the new suite fails (module not found). Implemented, only under write_paths: (1) `__harness__/processDeath/register.js` — a Node `-r` hook that compiles the shipping TypeScript with the app's own Babel config and maps `react-native` → `reactNativeStub.ts` (Platform/NativeModules.PickleVideoCapture/AppState only; the media stub re-reads the fixture file and returns the real SHA-256/byte verification shape) and `@op-engineering/op-sqlite` → `durableSqlite.ts` (file-backed `node:sqlite` DatabaseSync behind the op-sqlite `execute/executeSync/transaction` interface, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT`, with a PD_KILL trigger that SIGKILLs the process before/after the Nth statement matching given SQL fragments); (2) `child.ts` — runs the SHIPPING code path unchanged: setActiveDataOwner → api session → getDb() schema open → snapshot as-found → savePendingCapture (launch 1) → configureSyncRuntime/triggerOutboxSync (journal recovery) → snapshot after-recovery → prepareOriginalCaptureAnalysis → runOriginalCaptureAnalysis (real @pickle/evaluation inference on a synthetic swing) → triggerOutboxSync drain → final snapshot, printed as a `PD_REPORT` JSON line; fetch is wrapped only to add the http kill trigger (before send / after the server committed and answered); (3) `ratingService.ts` — loopback HTTP server mirroring supabase/functions/api idempotency (permit reserve by idempotencyKey, same-outcome finalize replay, shots:sync replay-accept, permit consumption) and recording every request; (4) `harness.ts` — spawns launch 1 (with kill) and launch 2 (same DB file, same server, proposed new operation id) and parses exit code/signal/PD_KILL marker/report; (5) `killPoints.ts` — 12 deterministic points: capture_saved, operation_insert_mid_transaction, seal_update_mid_transaction, attempt_insert_mid_transaction, attempt_admitted_before_reserve_request, permit_reserved_response_lost (server has the permit, client never saw the response), permit_update_mid_transaction, commit_shot_inserted_mid_transaction, commit_outbox_inserted_mid_transaction, result_committed_before_sync_request, sync_accepted_response_lost (server has the shot, client never saw the ack), receipt_inserted_mid_transaction. The Jest suite asserts per point: launch 1 really died by SIGKILL at that step; as-found durable state matches (statements inside an uncommitted transaction are rolled back — e.g. the record/shot/outbox commit is all-or-nothing); after relaunch every row is owner-scoped, there is exactly ONE logical operation (a surviving operation is continued under its original id, never re-created) and exactly ONE attempt; for pre-admission and post-commit kills the end state is exactly one analysis record = one local_shot = one server shot, zero outbox rows, exactly one shot.sync receipt, exactly one server permit (finalized scored) and, when the result was already on disk, `replayed: true` with the same analysisId; for kills after an attempt was admitted but before the result committed the shipping journal HOLDS: the same permit is released `cancelled` under the same reservation key (every reserve request the relaunch made reused it), zero results/outbox/receipts/server shots, no second permit, outcome `unavailable`/`recovery_pending` — no fabricated score and nothing consumed. Note on the manifest wording 'exactly one durable result and one outbox entry': that is asserted for every point where a result can legitimately exist; for the five held points the product invariant 'ambiguous commitment ⇒ HOLD/recover' means the correct durable outcome is zero results and zero outbox rows with the permit reconciled, which the suite asserts explicitly instead of forcing a score. implement.approach: Started from BASE_SHA 42291369 on a fresh branch devin/pp/w02-03/impl-r2. Commit 1 (93bb2606) cherry-picks the round-1 regression suite unchanged (test-first; it fails on BASE_SHA because the harness does not exist). Commit 2 (5a4bb26e) cherry-picks the round-1 harness (child.ts, durableSqlite.ts, killPoints.ts, killSwitch.ts, ratingService.ts, reactNativeStub.ts, register.js, report.ts — all sound per the round-1 review) with ONE change in harness.ts launchChild(): the child is spawned with `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning` ahead of `-r register.js child.ts`. VERIFIED (node -e) that on Node 22.23.2 this silences exactly the node:sqlite ExperimentalWarning while a DeprecationWarning (and any error) still reaches stderr, so the suite's strict `expect(launch.stderr).toBe('')` on every successful launch keeps its full strength; the flag is a no-op on Node 24 (no warning emitted there). No test was weakened, no assertion filtered, no shipping src/ file touched.
